tasks.title: Security: re-apply the lock, encryption and dark mode on current main
tasks.prompt:
The Tijori React Native app already has a completed security change set on the branch 'jules-6136906809176550882-a55b9ffa' (app lock with passcode + biometric, encryption at rest, real Settings, and a dark/light theme). That branch now CONFLICTS with main, so it cannot be merged.

Task: re-apply that same work cleanly on top of the CURRENT main, and open a fresh pull request.

How: read the files on branch 'jules-6136906809176550882-a55b9ffa' (src/ThemeContext.tsx, src/PasscodeSetupScreen.tsx, src/storage/, src/screens.tsx, src/components.tsx, App.tsx, package.json) to see what was intended. Then integrate those changes with the current main - main already includes Documents, the password generator/vault health, and polish work, so do NOT overwrite those; combine them.

Keep the existing visual language. Make sure the lock really gates the app, data is encrypted at rest, Settings actually works (biometric toggle, change passcode, auto-lock timing defaulting to 1 minute, and a light/dark switch), and the theme context is used across the screens.

Housekeeping: no temporary or patch files (.diff, .patch, .orig, .rej, .bak or editor backups), and no reasoning or thinking-out-loud comments in the code.

Constraints: TypeScript; npm run typecheck, npm run lint and npm test must pass. react-native-keychain and crypto-js are already allowed.

tasks.title: Documents: expiry dates, expiring soon, and document packs
tasks.prompt:
Continue the Tijori React Native app. Build on the existing Documents section (src/DocumentsScreen.tsx, src/DocumentSheet.tsx, src/storage/) - read it first and extend it rather than recreating it.

Task:
1. Give each document an optional expiry date, using a date picker (reuse src/Calendar.tsx).
2. Add an 'Expiring soon' section at the top of the Documents screen listing documents expiring within the next 90 days, with the number of days remaining. No push notifications.
3. Add document packs: a small set of ready-made checklists (for example Passport application, Bank KYC, Driving licence) showing which required document types the user already has and which are missing. A pack is satisfied when every required type is present.
4. Add unit tests for any new storage logic.

Keep the existing visual language and keep the change additive.

Housekeeping: no temporary or patch files (.diff, .patch, .orig, .rej, .bak or editor backups), and no reasoning or thinking-out-loud comments in the code.

Constraints: TypeScript; npm run typecheck, npm run lint and npm test must pass; do not add new dependencies.
